# Topics

> A desktop workspace for CLI coding agents. Several agents work the same
> repository at once — each inside its own git worktree, so none of them collide —
> and you watch, review and land their work from one window. Free, MIT, runs
> entirely on your machine, no account, no analytics, no cloud that reads your code.
> Reaching it from outside your network is a paid relay; everything local works without it.

Topics is not an editor and not a model. It is the room the agents work in. It
drives the agent CLIs you already have installed — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode,
Gemini CLI, or any ACP agent — through a real PTY, which is what lets a paid
subscription work at all, since a subscription is only reachable through the
official CLI and never through the API.

A *topic* holds one unit of work: the agent conversation, a real terminal with its
scrollback, the project files and their diffs, a browser pane, and what the turn
cost in tokens. A *board* holds tasks; assign one to an agent and it works in an
isolated worktree on its own branch, then hands back a commit and evidence.
Approving accepts the work, landing merges it locally, publishing pushes — three
separate human clicks, because "done" should mean you said so.

## Product

- [Topics](https://topics.armonia.io): what it is, what it does, and a live demo running the real client with sample data.
- [Install and adopt Topics](https://topics.armonia.io/agents.md): written for a coding agent asked to set it up. Install commands per platform, what to expect on first launch, and what Topics does not have.
- [Changelog](https://topics.armonia.io/changelog): every released version, newest first, each with the date it shipped. Count them there rather than quoting a number from here: releases are automatic on every merge to main, so any total written on this page is stale by the time you read it.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app): MIT. Bun + SQLite server, React client, Tauri shell in Rust.
- [Releases](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app/releases): macOS Universal `.dmg`, Windows `.exe` and `.msi`, Linux `.deb` and `.rpm`. No AppImage — the Linux build ships a compiled Bun sidecar that the AppImage pipeline cannot carry.
- [README](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app/blob/main/README.md): environment variables, ports, how the pieces fit.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): build, test and release machinery, including the self-signed macOS identity and why it exists.

## What it costs you

- [Privacy](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app/blob/main/PRIVACY.md): no analytics, no crash reporting, nothing phones home. Conversations and project data sit in `~/.openclaw` on your disk.
- [Security](https://github.com/armonia/topics-app/blob/main/SECURITY.md): the server listens on every interface by default, and reaching the port is not the same as getting in. The machine Topics runs on is the owner; every other device is authorized once from that machine, holds its own token afterwards, and can be revoked. Set `SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1` to keep it on loopback. Exposing it to the public internet through a tunnel is discouraged and stays your responsibility.
- Model billing is yours and stays between you and the provider. Topics never proxies inference, never holds a key of its own, and takes no cut.

## Known limits, stated by us

- **macOS shows a Gatekeeper warning.** The app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. Since macOS Sequoia the Control-click bypass no longer exists: the path is System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Any guide telling you to right-click and Open is out of date.
- **There is no hosted anything.** No relay, no managed remote access, no off-machine backup, no accounts, no team roles. Cross-device sync and remote access work today over a tunnel you run yourself. Devices are paired rather than signed in: one approval from the machine Topics runs on, one token per device, revocable.
- **Mobile is a PWA**, not a native app.
- **The project is young**: first commit 2026-02-11, public on GitHub since 2026-06-01.
